Case Study UX · Health Design · Capstone 2021

The Cyster Community

A holistic PCOS management platform combining social accountability, gamification, smart nutrition tracking, and a sensor-connected plate — designed to help young Indian women build a sustainable active lifestyle.

Role
Solo Designer
End-to-end
Timeline
6 months
Capstone project
Platform
Mobile App
+ IoT Product
Institution
NMIMS
School of Design
1 in 5
Indian women affected by PCOS
10
Users tested — 8 PCOS women + 2 gynaecologists
4
Pillars addressed — diet, exercise, sleep, stress
01 — The Problem

Motivation collapses without visible change

1 in 5 Indian women suffer from PCOS, yet no solution addresses all four management pillars holistically. Women lose motivation fast — especially when weight loss is slower with PCOS than without it.

02 — Framework

Four pillars. One broken system.

Research revealed four non-negotiable components of PCOS management. Applying Fogg's Behavioural Model exposed exactly why current solutions fail — exercise sits in the lowest motivation × highest difficulty quadrant.

03 — Ideation

Two concepts. One winning combination.

Three concepts were developed and tested. Concept 1 focused on community and gamification. Concept 3 introduced a smart portion-guide plate linked to a retreat reward system. User feedback shaped the final direction.

04 — Solution

The Cyster Community — app + smart plate

The final concept merges the two strongest ideas: a social gamified app with group accountability, and a sensor-equipped Kansa plate that auto-syncs food data. Together they address all four pillars without adding friction.

05 — Structure

Information architecture

A full IA was mapped before moving to screens — covering individual and group onboarding, five core app modules, a gamified points system, and the settings and community layers. Everything marked with an asterisk earns points.

06 — Key Journeys

Five journeys, all tested

Registration, meal plan, tiffin service, group training, and schedule tracking — each journey was prototyped, tested, and refined based on real user feedback.

07 — Product Design

The smart plate

A 30cm Kansa plate with hand-size portion sections and hidden load-cell sensors that wirelessly sync to the app — making food tracking frictionless. A physical nudge that builds portion awareness over time, even without the app open.

30cm diameter · 4cm height Kansa material Load cell sensors Bluetooth sync Hand-size portion guide
08 — Validation

Tested with users and experts

Eight PCOS women and two gynaecologists tested four key journeys plus the physical prototype. The community concept was unanimously favoured. The plate was described as impactful even before being used. Both gynaecologists confirmed the concept bridges a real market gap.

09 — Business Model

A value-driven model built to scale

Revenue from plate + tiffin subscriptions, dynamic pricing via gynaecologist referrals, and in-app advertising — with a roadmap toward medical data partnerships and expansion to tier-2 Indian cities.
